entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6048"/><div sID="gen9234" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6048"/><hi type="bold">8-15. However scrupulous in external worship, it was offered as if they conferred an obligation in giving God His own, and with a degrading view of Him as needing it [Psa 50:9-13]. Reproving them for such foolish and blasphemous notions, He teaches them to offer, or literally, "sacrifice," thanksgiving, and pay, or perform, their vows--</hi>that is, to bring, with the external symbolical service, the homage of the heart, and faith, penitence, and love. To this is added an invitation to seek, and a promise to afford, all needed help in trouble. <div eID="gen9234" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6049"/><div sID="gen9235" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6049"/><hi type="bold">16-20. the wicked--</hi>that is, the formalists, as now exposed, and who lead vicious lives (compare <reference osisRef="Rom.2.21">Ro 2:21</reference>, 23). They are unworthy to use even the words of God's law. Their hypocrisy and vice are exposed by illustrations from sins against the seventh, eighth, and ninth commandments. <div eID="gen9235" type="x-p"/>
